title: ICE is building a machine designed so no one can watch it
body: The Lever reports that ICE has quietly built a DNA bank. A new report from Georgetown Law's Center on Privacy and Technology found the Department of Homeland Security is now the single largest contributor to the FBI's DNA database. ICE submitted the DNA of almost 900,000 people in 2025, up from 16,392 in 2021. That is a more than 5,000 percent jump in four years. Most of these people are not suspected of any crime, and their genetic profiles stay in the FBI system indefinitely.

That was one of three moves in the same week. 404 Media reports ICE plans to pay the data broker LexisNexis another $6.7 million to feed personal records into Palantir, a system built to help find and deport people. And The Lever finds DHS spent $2.2 billion buying four detention centers outright from private prison giant CoreCivic. Owning the buildings is the point. Federal ownership lets ICE claim immunity from state oversight and from lawsuits over abuse, even as detention deaths rise.

Line it up and it is one project. Collect the DNA, buy the data, own the cages, and put all of it beyond the reach of anyone who could ask a hard question. This is not enforcement getting more efficient. It is a surveillance operation being built in the exact spot where oversight used to sit.
